name: CountBench
intro: CountBench是一个用于评估视觉语言模型（VLM）对象计数能力的新型图像-文本计数基准。它通过自动创建反事实示例来改进VLM的定量理解，并鼓励模型区分正确和不正确的计数描述。该基准旨在评估模型对图像中对象数量的理解。
build_method: LAION-400M 英文数字词 two 至 ten 过滤，现成目标检测器最大类别计数匹配，每个数量预平衡至 100–200 条，人工核对清晰可见物体后重平衡为每个数量 60 条
metric: 计数准确率 = mean[预测数量 = 真实数量]；平均绝对计数偏差 = mean|预测数量 − 真实数量|
eval_feature: 测试集与计数训练集无重叠, 九分类零样本图文相似度
build_method_en: Filter LAION-400M captions for spelled counts two through ten; require the count to match the most prevalent class from an off-the-shelf detector; pre-balance each count to 100–200 candidates; manually verify clearly visible objects; then rebalance to 60 pairs per count
eval_feature_en: No overlap with counting training set, nine-way zero-shot image-text similarity
intro_en: CountBench is a novel image-text counting benchmark designed to evaluate the object counting ability of vision-language models (VLMs). It improves VLMs' quantitative understanding by automatically generating counterfactual examples and encourages models to distinguish between correct and incorrect counting descriptions. This benchmark aims to assess models' comprehension of object quantities in images.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2302.12066v1 §4 and §5.1 and official repository full commit 2c573a8d8fa0b6c2ea5cfdd3f914a6b0ed5dd88a. The pinned CountBench.json contains exactly 540 rows: 60 examples for each true count from two through ten. LAION-400M captions are filtered to spelled counts two–ten and visible-count usage; an off-the-shelf detector retains cases where that count matches the most prevalent detected class. The very uneven candidate pool (over 158K for two versus about 100 for ten) is pre-balanced to 100–200 per count, manually checked for clearly visible objects, and rebalanced to 60 per count. The final set is test-only and does not overlap the counting training set. Evaluation builds nine captions per image, selects the count with highest CLIP-B/32 or BASIC-S image-text similarity, and reports mean[Predicted Count = True Count] plus mean|Predicted Count − True Count|. The paper and pinned official release disclose no benchmark-specific dedup stage; none is invented here.
